question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation to isolate the logarithmic term:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{log}_{2}⁡(x+12)}{2} & =4 \\ {log}_{2}⁡(x+12) & =8\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The base of the logarithm is $2,$ so we use this base for the exponentiation as well:

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{2}⁡(x+12) & =8 \\ {2}^{{log}_{2}⁡(x+12)} & ={2}^{8}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we get ${2}^{{log}_{2}⁡(x+12)}=x+12.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}x+12 & ={2}^{8} \\ x+12 & =256 \\ x & =244.\end{aligned}
$$
